headline.text: In Varsinais-Suomen hyvinvointialue, crude recorded curative, life-prolonging, and symptomatic treatment shares and MDT recording lag behind national values, while 43.1% have no treatment record within 12 months.

details.text: Across overlapping treatment categories that are crude and not adjusted for age or stage, curative treatment is 24.3% (95% CI 22.1–26.6; n=349/1437) versus 27.0% nationally, life-prolonging treatment is 9.7% (95% CI 8.3–11.4; n=140/1437) versus 30.4%, and symptomatic treatment is 30.8% (95% CI 28.5–33.3; n=443/1437) versus 39.5%, with all 95% confidence intervals excluding the national values.

In figures digitised from Kuva 16 (precision about ±0.5 percentage points), the curative gap holds after age adjustment for men at 22.7% versus 26.7% nationally (confidence interval bar hidden inside the dot, half-width < ~3.3 percentage points), but not for women at 27.4% (95% CI 23.1–31.8), whose 95% confidence interval includes the national 26.9%.

Meanwhile, 43.1% (95% CI 40.5–45.6; n=619/1437) have no treatment record within 12 months compared with 27.5% nationally (4089/14873), and a multidisciplinary team (MDT) meeting is recorded for 1.6% (95% CI 1.1–2.4; n=23/1437) compared with 6.0% nationally (893/14873), with these 95% confidence intervals excluding the national values.

headline.text: The county's high share of patients with no treatment record within 12 months suggests unrecorded care, while public data omit stage for ~48% of patients and lack pathway timestamps.

details.text: Because having no treatment record within 12 months mixes untreated patients and unrecorded treatment, we infer from the 43.1% county share (versus 27.5% nationally) as a data-quality signal that low recorded treatment shares may partly reflect unrecorded treatment, whereas a journal article shows hospital discharge register concordance of about 90% for diagnoses only.

Similarly, MDT records measure recording practice rather than care because specialist procedures enter HILMO only from direct patient contacts, and stage at diagnosis is missing for ~48% of new patients nationally, preventing stage adjustment of county treatment shares.

Public data exclude outpatient primary care and occupational health visits and lack dates for symptoms, referrals, imaging waits, specialist visits, and treatment start, though preliminary, unpublished national figures show 155 days on average from symptoms to treatment in Finland (versus 107 in Sweden and 67 in Denmark), including 56 patient, 41 primary care, and 58 specialist care days.

headline.text: Varsinais-Suomen hyvinvointialue should prioritise auditing treatment, stage, and MDT recording, tracking pathway handovers using THL Ohjaus 21/2016 definitions, and standardising referral criteria and diagnostic care coordination.

details.text: Given the 43.1% share with no treatment record within 12 months, 1.6% MDT recording, and incomplete lung cancer data collection nationally, the county should audit and publish recording completeness for treatments, stage, and MDT coding using uniform recording instructions, while the roadmap plans a national quality registry with 90% coverage including stage.

Because the Health Care Act sets no legal maximum time for a cancer suspicion and Finland lacks uniform national access-time monitoring, the county should monitor referral-to-treatment handovers using THL guidance Ohjaus 21/2016 definitions for 16 cancers now, as the Filha programme's diagnostics recommendation with recommended time limits is due before the 2030 mid-term evaluation.

Because mentor insight indicates that a weak referral gets a lower urgency rating in specialist care and occupational health gets patients to specialist care faster, the county should adopt standardised primary care referral criteria, symptom-based models, and a designated care coordinator now, while the roadmap plans national coordinator guidelines in 2026–2028 for county adoption in 2029–2031.

q:4e702a20fe.claim_text: Finland has no unified national system to steer the drafting of cancer-specific treatment recommendations, or the implementation and monitoring of care pathways based on them (quality and effectiveness targets/indicators, including access to care, and cancer-specific and generic PROMs). Existing recommendations and pathways, and the targets and indicators to be monitored, are not coordinated nationally. This maintains regional inequality in the availability and effectiveness of cancer care.
q:4e702a20fe.quote: Suomessa ei ole yhtenäistä kansallista järjestelmää, joka ohjaisi syöpäkohtaisten hoitosuositusten laatimista sekä niihin perustuvien hoitoketjujen toteutusta ja seurantaa (laatu- ja vaikuttavuustavoitteet/indikaattorit, mukaan lukien hoitoonpääsy sekä syöpäkohtaiset ja geneeriset PROM-vointimittarit). Olemassa olevia hoitosuosituksia ja -ketjuja sekä seurattavia tavoitteita ja indikaattoreita ei koordinoida kansallisella tasolla. Tämä ylläpitää alueellista eriarvoisuutta syövän hoidon saatavuudessa ja vaikuttavuudessa.
q:4e702a20fe.quote_en: Finland does not have a uniform national system to guide the preparation of cancer-specific clinical guidelines and the implementation and monitoring of care pathways based on them (quality and effectiveness targets/indicators, including access to care as well as cancer-specific and generic PROM well-being measures). Existing clinical guidelines and care pathways as well as monitored targets and indicators are not coordinated at the national level. This maintains regional inequality in the availability and effectiveness of cancer care.
